g.text: Example 1 · regular: a = 6 cheese, b = 4 sausage

text.tspan: The pool: 6 cheese slices, 4 sausage slices.
Every slice must be used. No “equal” rule anywhere!
Each sandwich needs ≥ 1 surplus cheese → k ≤ 2
The “+1” is what makes cheese strictly greater.
Here it happens to be 2 + 2 sausage and 3 + 3 cheese.

g.text: Example 2 · irregular: a = 7 cheese, b = 5 sausage

text.tspan: Can unequal sandwiches still work? Let’s see.
Surplus is the tight pile: k ≤ 2 (sausage alone allows k ≤ 5)
So 5 sausage slices must be shared by 2 sandwiches.
Split sausage unevenly: 3 on one sandwich, 2 on the other.
Cheese = sausage + 1, so 4 and 3. Not identical, and that is allowed!
Unequal cheese (4, 3) and unequal sausage (3, 2): every sandwich still wins.
